Emma — thanks for the clear asks. I'm attaching a preliminary forecast (zenkamp_q3q4_qps_token_forecast.xlsx) and a sizing note. High level summary up front:

- Forecasted baseline: current production averages 180 qps with 450k tokens/day. Zenkamp expects a 2x growth trajectory by Q4 driven by new conversational triage flows and expanded embedding usage; peak bursts near 350 qps expected during business hours.
- Recommended reserved pool: 8x A100-80GB equiv GPUs (or 16x T4v2-class inference units) for predictable throughput and KV cache locality. This maps to ~10k qps sustained of smaller models; for your mixed workload (long-form summarization + chat) the 8x recommendation gives ~95th percentile headroom with batching.
- Throughput guarantees: propose committed SLA for 99th percentile token latency under provisioned capacity; fallback plan uses a lower-cost variant model with auto-failover.

I'll let Marissa and Karthik add pricing and a redline for SLA language. Proposed next step: 30-minute sync Thursday to walk the workbook.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Technical notes to justify the 8x A100 recommendation and capacity safety margins:

- Workload mix: 60% short-chat (avg 60 tokens per request, 25% streaming), 25% long-form summarization (avg 1200 tokens), 15% embedding/rerank. Weighted avg token per request ~300 tokens.
- Token/sec expectation at 350 qps peak -> 105k tokens/sec peak. Our internal microbench: A100-80GB equiv sustains ~18k tokens/sec for this mixed model family with batching optimizations. 8x gives ~144k tokens/sec aggregate headroom.
- KV cache: recommend sticky routing to preserve KV locality; warm caches pre-warmed during business hours to avoid cold-start spikes for long-form tasks.
- Canary plan: deploy 2 GPUs as canary in week 1, ramp to 4 for week 2, then flip remaining 4 on day-of committed capacity—this reduces risk and validates batching profiles.

I'll include these benchmarks in the workbook and can run a short synthetic load from Redwood test harness against a sample prompt set if you'd like.

Karthik
Applied ML / Solutions Engineering

Emma — great questions. Quick answers ahead of Thursday's call and attached docs:

1) Multi-region mapping: recommended baseline is 8x A100 in primary (us-west) and a mirrored 4x A100 pool in eu-west as failover (async KV replica + cross-region prefix caching). Cost delta for the mirrored pool is ~45% of the primary committed price (we include warm standby pricing option in the PDF).

2) Sensitivity table: included in zenkamp_q3q4_qps_token_forecast.xlsx tab 'Sensitivity'. Highlights: +30% growth -> keep 8x primary, add single canary GPU earlier; +80% growth -> recommended move to 12x primary (scales linearly for token-bound paths) and 6x mirror. Incremental cost: +$28k/mo for moving 8->12.

3) SLA paragraph (draft): "Redwood will provide a 99th-percentile token latency target of <= 220ms for provisioned models under committed reserved capacity. In cases where sustained burst traffic exceeds provisioned capacity, Redwood will execute configured fallback policies (model variant or burst pool) and notify the customer per the incident escalation path." See proposed-sla-delta.docx for redline.

Action items for Thursday: Marissa to present pricing table variants; Karthik to walk the sensitivity workbook and proposed canary timeline; Ben to confirm procurement billing template and contract language tweaks.

If anyone wants the synthetic load run before the call, reply-all with preferred time windows and a representative prompt set.

—Olga
